payload.blocks: Phase 4 of plan 261124-2143-head-lifecycle-events (row p-tyowvhthul) and the phases after it; phases 1-3 go on without it.
payload.headline: Lead slots: count a lead waiting outside as free, or raise the lane count from measured capacity?

parts.cause: Admission counts every live lead against the fixed supervisor.maxLeads; nothing tells a waiting lead from a working one, and nothing raises the limit when the machine has room.

options.does: A running plan whose open phases are all parked on another party (the lead's existing park record) counts its live lead as waiting, not working; admission compares working leads with maxLeads.
options.gain: Uses data that already exists; small change in the supervision crate; the ready plan on 2026-11-23 would have started.
options.harm: A waiting lead's session still uses memory, so live sessions can exceed maxLeads by the number of waiting leads.
options.label: A waiting lead does not hold a working slot

options.cost: A larger phase that must be replanned with its own measures.
options.does: Admission computes the lane count from provider seats, free memory and free disk at each wake instead of the fixed maxLeads.
options.gain: Uses the machine fully and also guards against the OOM and full-disk cases seen the same day.
options.harm: Needs new capacity inputs and thresholds that do not exist yet; a wrong measure admits too many or too few.
options.label: Raise the lane count from measured capacity

parts.recommendation: A waiting lead does not hold a working slot: it fixes the case that happened with data already recorded; capacity-based lanes can be a later row if memory pressure shows up.

scope.allows: Phase 4 builds only the picked rule, and phase 5 writes it in the supervision spec.
scope.forbids: Changing maxLeads defaults, provider seat rules or how a plan becomes ready.

parts.what: On 2026-11-23 maxLeads was 2 and one slot was held by a lead sitting in a measurement window with no unit running, so a ready plan was not admitted. The plan must pick one rule for admission.
